item: 1.10 Markdown inline emphasis (2026-10-10): bold that wraps an italic (`**Garlic (*Allium sativum*)**`) renders as <b> with an <i> inside, not as literal `**`
branch: onClaudeEvent text_delta → renderMd → mdBlocks paragraph branch → inlineMd (20-markdown.js): the bold pass runs before the italic pass, so the bold regex must admit single `*` characters inside the pair; the italic pass then finds the inner pair with the <b> already in place. The same inlineMd serves headings, table cells, replay (55-replay.js), plan cards and the side question.
provenance: Step 1's text is REAL: the assistant paragraphs of the user's 2026-10-08 conversation (_local/2026-10-08/949f51ad-ee45-4ef3-a5c1-e7250632e747.jsonl, CLI 2.1.276) read BY KEY from the `assistant` text block, verbatim — the user screenshotted them rendering as `**Lashuna / Rasona — Garlic (Allium sativum)**` with the species italic and the asterisks printed. Frame shapes are fixture 86's; nothing new is claimed about the CLI. Steps 2-4 are guards and the reverse nesting (italic wrapping bold), written from CommonMark, not from a transcript. PRE-FIX MECHANISM (read from the code, confirmed by the control run): inlineMd's bold regex was /\*\*([^*]+)\*\*/ — a single `*` anywhere inside the pair made the whole bold fail to match, and the italic pass then paired only the inner single asterisks. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-10-10 against the sandbox still serving the pre-change webview (started before the edit, fixture written first): 6 passed, 6 failed — every guard passed (heading, two italics, three plain bolds, reverse nesting), every DISCRIMINATING assert failed: step 1 read 0 <b>, 0 b>i, a null first bold and a literal `**` at index 18; step 4 read ONE bold whose text was ' and ' — the old regex paired the `)**` closing the first phrase with the `**` opening C, so the greedy mis-pairing is real, not just a missing bold.

delta.text:
## Strongest evidence

**Lashuna / Rasona — Garlic (*Allium sativum*)**
The best-supported item on this list. Meta-analyses of RCTs show aged garlic extract lowers systolic BP by ~8 mmHg in people who are already hypertensive — comparable to a first-line drug at low dose. Works via nitric oxide and hydrogen sulfide pathways. Raw garlic works too, though dosing is less consistent. Caution: it has genuine antiplatelet effects, so it matters if you're on aspirin, clopidogrel, or warfarin.

**Japa — Hibiscus (*Hibiscus sabdariffa*)**
Multiple RCTs, ~7 mmHg systolic reduction over 4–6 weeks as a tea (2–3 cups/day). Mild diuretic effect. Cheap, safe, easy. One of the few where the trial evidence is reasonably clean.
